edges.description: The expressed mutant or dosage-altered SOX10 protein disrupts SOX10-dependent neural crest and extraneural crest glial and otic transcriptional networks.
Impaired SOX10 transcriptional activity in Schwann cells and oligodendrocytes disrupts central and peripheral myelin formation.
Impaired activation of the RET enhancer by SOX10 and PAX3 disrupts enteric neural crest colonization of the distal bowel.
Dominant-negative SOX10 impairs transactivation of the MITF promoter, perturbing melanocyte differentiation.
SOX10 dysfunction impairs survival of cochlear progenitors and glial development of the cochleovestibular ganglia.
Peripheral Schwann cell dysmyelination causes demyelinating peripheral neuropathy.
Oligodendrocyte dysmyelination causes diffuse central white matter hypomyelination.
Distal bowel hypoganglionosis, aganglionosis, or enteric neuropathy produces Hirschsprung disease or chronic intestinal pseudo-obstruction.
Schwann cell dysmyelination directly causes peripheral neuropathy.
Peripheral demyelinating neuropathy contributes to diffuse neonatal and infantile hypotonia.
Loss of peripheral myelinated nerve conduction impairs deep tendon reflex arcs, producing hyporeflexia or areflexia.
Central dysmyelinating leukodystrophy impairs psychomotor and cognitive maturation, causing global developmental delay.
Central white matter hypomyelination contributes to central hypotonia.
Central white matter dysmyelination causes pyramidal tract dysfunction and spasticity.
Central dysmyelination disrupts cerebellar and spinocerebellar white matter pathways, producing ataxia.
Central dysmyelination of ocular motor pathways causes congenital nystagmus.
Enteric ganglion cell deficiency causes distal bowel aganglionosis (Hirschsprung disease).
Neurogenic enteric nervous system dysfunction or hypoganglionosis causes chronic intestinal pseudo-obstruction.
Severe intestinal aganglionosis or hypoganglionosis predisposes to recurrent enterocolitis.
Melanocyte deficiency and impaired melanin synthesis cause cutaneous hypopigmentation.
Defective neural crest melanocyte development in the iris stroma causes iris hypopigmentation.
Defective follicular melanocyte differentiation causes hair hypopigmentation.
Inner ear developmental abnormality directly causes bilateral sensorineural hearing impairment.
Disrupted placodal otic vesicle morphogenesis causes hypoplasia, dysplasia, or agenesis of the semicircular canals.
Disrupted otic vesicle and cochlear progenitor survival leads to inner ear hypoplasia.

nodes.description: PCWH-associated truncating SOX10 variants (typically located in the last coding exon, exon 5, or the last 45 nucleotides of the penultimate exon, exon 4) escape nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD) and produce an expressed C-terminally truncated SOX10 protein that retains the HMG DNA-binding domain but lacks normal transactivation capacity, exerting dominant-negative interference over wild-type SOX10. Additional pathogenic mechanisms capable of producing the PCW/PCWH spectrum include non-stop (C-terminal extension) variants that generate a deleterious tryptophan-arginine (WR) domain with toxic gain-of-function or dominant-additive effects, specific missense variants (such as Gln174/Pro175 variants that form nuclear paraspeckle foci with p54NRB/NONO and sequester wild-type SOX10, or dimerization-domain variants), and 22q13.1 duplications encompassing SOX10.

evidence.snippet: Here we report that although all nonsense and frameshift mutations that cause premature termination of translation generate truncated SOX10 proteins with potent dominant-negative activity, the more severe disease phenotype, PCWH, is realized only when the mutant mRNAs escape the nonsense-mediated decay (NMD) pathway.
